content.user_title: Estimate Market Size with TAM, SAM, and SOM
content.value_statement: Market sizing is hard when sources, assumptions, and methods are scattered. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through defensible TAM, SAM, and SOM analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains TAM, SAM, and SOM definitions with practical examples.
Provides top-down, bottom-up, and value-theory market sizing formulas.
Guides source selection across industry reports, public data, filings, and customer research.
Shows how to apply geographic, product, segment, and adoption filters.
Includes investor and strategy presentation structures for market sizing work.
Provides a complete SaaS market sizing example.
limitations: Does not verify live market data without user-provided sources or browsing support.
Requires assumptions about customer counts, pricing, and adoption rates.
Cannot replace paid research reports or expert validation.
Outputs depend on the quality and recency of source data.

use_cases.title: Prepare Investor Market Slides
use_cases.description: Build a clear TAM, SAM, and SOM story with documented assumptions and conservative capture rates.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Market Segments
use_cases.description: Compare customer segments by addressable revenue, serviceability, and realistic near-term opportunity.

use_cases.title: Validate Market Research Models
use_cases.description: Check market sizing calculations against source quality, segment definitions, and triangulation logic.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Market Size
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis for a new startup idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate TAM, SAM, and SOM for my product: [product]. Target customers are [customer segment], geography is [region], and price is [price]. State assumptions clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Bottom-Up Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate analysis using customer counts and pricing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use a bottom-up method to size [market]. Include customer segments, estimated customer counts, annual revenue per customer, penetration assumptions, and TAM, SAM, and SOM.

prompt_templates.title: Triangulate Multiple Methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Size [market] using top-down, bottom-up, and value-theory methods. Compare results, explain differences, and recommend the most defensible range.

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test Investor Assumptions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before fundraising or board materials.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this market sizing analysis: [paste analysis]. Find weak assumptions, missing sources, aggressive SOM claims, and changes needed for an investor presentation.

output_examples.input: Size the market for AI email marketing software for North American e-commerce brands.
output_examples.output: A TAM, SAM, and SOM summary with customer segments, geographic filters, pricing assumptions, and conservative capture rates.

output_examples.input: Check whether my marketplace SOM estimate is realistic for year five.
output_examples.output: A validation note comparing capture rate, competition, resources, and go-to-market assumptions against typical new entrant ranges.

output_examples.input: Create an investor-ready market sizing narrative from my source list.
output_examples.output: A concise market definition, source-backed sizing range, key assumptions, and risks to disclose in the presentation.

best_practices: Start with a precise market definition before calculating any market size.
Use bottom-up analysis as the primary model when customer and pricing data are available.
Document every source, assumption, filter, and capture rate.
anti_patterns: Claiming the full global category as serviceable without geographic or product filters.
Using one outdated report without triangulating against other sources.
Projecting high SOM without evidence for distribution, resources, and competitive advantage.

faq.question: What does this skill help calculate?
faq.answer: It helps estimate TAM, SAM, and SOM for startup and business opportunities.

faq.question: Which market sizing methods are included?
faq.answer: It covers top-down, bottom-up, and value-theory approaches.

faq.question: Can it create investor-facing output?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for investor presentations, assumptions, source notes, and market sizing narratives.

faq.question: Does it fetch current market data automatically?
faq.answer: No. It needs user-provided data or browsing support to verify current figures.

faq.question: Is it useful for niche markets?
faq.answer: Yes. Bottom-up and value-theory methods are designed for niche or emerging markets.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide customer segments, geography, pricing, source links, competitor context, and any existing research.
